observation.visible_scene: An artificial whitewater course enclosed by stacked blue plastic barriers, with spectators on an elevated platform in the background and a 'Walgreens' banner at the upper left. A small inflatable craft made of two blue cylindrical pontoons carries two helmeted paddlers in pink shirts through turbulent green water with white foam; a yellow double-bladed paddle is held overhead.
visible_changes: At the start (frames 1-6) both paddlers sit upright in the level craft, gripping the yellow paddle raised above their heads as the craft bobs in the rapids.
Around frames 7-12 the craft begins to lean and roll to one side; the paddlers' bodies tilt with it while the paddle is still held up.
In frames 13-17 the roll continues into a capsize: the white underside and blue pontoons of the craft swing up out of the water and the paddlers are displaced into the water beside it.
From frames 18-30 the craft lies inverted/on its side on the surface, drifting, with one paddler's boot sticking up and the other paddler in the water still holding the paddle vertically.
In frames 31-41 the overturned craft settles flatter on the water and drifts toward the left of the view; the paddlers remain separated from and alongside it.
The background (spectator platform, ramp, and the left-side Walgreens banner) shifts position across the sequence, indicating the camera pans left to follow the drifting craft.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the craft to roll (wave, paddle stroke, or contact) is not shown before the tilt begins.
Whether the paddlers right the craft, recover, or continue downstream is not shown after the segment ends.
uncertain_details: The exact split between the craft's own drift and the camera's leftward pan is hard to disentangle from the background shift alone.
The precise craft type (inflatable raft vs. pontoon kayak) and the position of the second paddler during the late drift are partly occluded by foam and the inverted hull.
